findings.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 — P1 confidence 100: `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` followed by `data: { key }` persists the parser's `{ success: true, data: ... }` envelope instead of the credential fields, so the next GoogleCalendarService construction passes an object without top-level tokens to `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` at line 75 and rejects a credential immediately after a successful refresh.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62 — P1 confidence 100: `const appCredential = await prisma.credential.findFirst({` selects by only `userId: reqBody.userId` and `appId: appMetadata.slug`, so syncing a second Google or Outlook account overwrites the first matching account's credentials instead of updating the intended account, while the existing OAuth callbacks create separate credentials per installation and the request schema contains no account or credential identifier to disambiguate them.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:78 — P2 confidence 75: Updating an existing credential with only `key: keys` preserves its previous `invalid: true` state after valid replacement tokens arrive, so credential sync cannot restore an installation marked invalid by the Google refresh path at packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:115.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75 — Advisory P2 confidence 100: The unconditional `const response = await fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", {` makes every new Salesforce client depend on a successful token exchange and database write even with an unexpired access token, so an OAuth endpoint outage disables otherwise usable Salesforce sessions; eagerly ensuring freshness is the strongest justification, but the subsequent jsforce connection already receives both access and refresh tokens, and deleting this eager exchange/update block and its otherwise-unused schema removes the extra dependency and request per client construction.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:42 — Advisory P2 confidence 100: `select: { id: true, members: { select: { userId: true } } }` materializes every member of a team on each OAuth installation even though the result is consumed only by `if (!team)`, making installation database transfer and allocation grow with team size; confirming membership is the strongest justification, but the existing `members: { some: { ... } }` predicate already performs that check, so deleting the selected `members` relation eliminates the unnecessary collection and its processing.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75 — [P1, confidence 75] `const response = await fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", {` omits the new credential-sync refresh route for Salesforce, so self-hosters enabling `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` still send the locally stored refresh token directly to Salesforce and cannot refresh credentials whose refresh token remains in the parent application.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:5 — [P2, confidence 100] `if (APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId) {` introduces distinct shared-user, native-user, and team-credential refresh paths without any test changes or recorded verification of their provider response parsing and persisted token fields, leaving this credential-sync change without evidence that its new end-to-end behavior works.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:96 — [P1, confidence 100] `await prisma.credential.update({` references `prisma` without any import or declaration in this module, failing TypeScript compilation and throwing ReferenceError after a successful Salesforce token refresh when type checking is bypassed.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 — [P1; confidence 100] `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` followed by `data: { key }` persists the `{ success: true, data: ... }` validation envelope instead of credentials after an ordinary Google refresh, so the next service construction fails `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` and disconnects the calendar even with sharing disabled.

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the new webhook endpoint at apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts uses findFirst with only userId and appId to locate credentials. Looking at the diff, lines 57-65 show: `await prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId: reqBody.userId, appId: appMetadata.slug } })`. The request schema (lines 9-14) only accepts userId, appSlug, and keys - no credential identifier. This means if a user has multiple credentials for the same app (e.g., two Google Calendar accounts), the sync would update the first matching credential rather than the intended one. The existing OAuth callbacks in the diff (e.g., googlecalendar/api/callback.ts) create new credentials via createOAuthAppCredential, allowing multiple accounts. This is a real correctness bug where credential sync could overwrite the wrong account's credentials.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for GoogleCalendarService.ts lines 93-97, the code changes from `const key = googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials);` to `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);`. The parseRefreshTokenResponse function (shown in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts) returns the result of `schema.safeParse(response)` which is a `{ success: boolean, data: ... }` object, not the parsed data itself. This is a real bug that breaks Google Calendar integration regardless of whether credential sharing is enabled.

However, the calling code at line 177 expects `hubspotRefreshToken` to be a `HubspotToken` object with properties like `expiresIn` and `accessToken`. When the Response object is returned instead, `hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn` will be undefined, causing `Math.round(Date.now() + hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn * 1000)` to produce NaN, and `hubspotRefreshToken.accessToken` will also be undefined. This is a real bug in the credential sharing mode.
